newsitem.title: USA: Maverick U.S. politician warns of Western collapse.
newsitem.headline: Maverick U.S. politician warns of Western collapse.

text.p: The man who defined the word maverick in U.S. politics is still going strong as the presidential election draws closer, warning that the end of Western civilisation is at hand.
Lyndon Larouche, perhaps the best-known conspiracy theorist in the United States, is not running for president this time -- as he did with spectacular lack of success in the 1980s.
The 74-year-old Democrat is backing U.S. President Bill Clinton, although without much enthusiasm, as "the only option available".

Larouche is more concerned about what he says is the impending collapse of the financial system and a nefarious, long-running plot to undermine nation states, closely linked to Britain's royal family.

"I'm more of a philosopher king than a politician. My concern is to make things happen, that's my businesss," he told Reuters in this small village amid Virginia's rolling hills, not far from Washington.
It all sounds unlikely but, in a country where bizarre views about UFOs or government cover-ups often seem to touch a chord, Larouche has won tens of thousands of votes in the past.
In articulate, measured tones, Larouche insists he has a unique grasp of current events and their importance.
"Now we're coming into the time of reality and that's where I dwell," he said. "I've seen that coming for a long time...The whole of blasted civilisation is being consumed."

Wearing tinted glasses and cowboy boots, Larouche talks about the world's ills. The child sex scandal in Belgium is linked to NATO and Russia is on the verge of dictatorship. Everywhere is in chaos and it is all linked together.
"The word is out all over the world, the financial system is gone...Either we're going to end the mess or we're going on to a new dark age," he said.
The remedy? Shut down the entire banking system and scrap global trade deals. Beyond that, it gets a bit complicated.
Larouche has been a busy man all his life. A management consultant in the shoe industry until the early 1950s, he then switched to economics and politics.

He has been involved in publishing, science and economic forecasting, claiming credit for developing the "Star Wars" missile defence system of the 1980s and for the push towards European Union integration.

According to U.S. prosecutors, he was too busy to deal properly with his taxes and was jailed in 1988, serving five years of a 15-year sentence. It was, Larouche says, part of a conspiracy to get him -- led by former U.S. Secretary of State Henry Kissinger.
Some political analysts have seen Larouche as a focus for disaffected voters, essentially in the same mould as Texas billionaire Ross Perot.
Larouche disagrees, labelling Perot as "a creation of the intelligence community".
He claims Communists and others have tried to have him killed. Asked whether he owns the house where the interview takes place, he smiles.
"No. My people move me around," he said. "It's standard procedure."
